lede: Simpletics is a men's hair styling brand founded in 2024 by Dillon Latham, best known for a Sea Salt Spray made with five ingredients. Its store ratings are good, but its Trustpilot page tells a rougher story. Here's what it sells, what buyers say on both, and who it suits.

parts: Simpletics is a real brand with a Shopify store, full policies and a 30-day money-back guarantee that covers opened products. Its Sea Salt Spray scores 4.3 out of 5 from 872 reviews on its own store, and the Texture Powder 4.3 from 215. But Trustpilot shows a TrustScore of 2 from 22 reviews, most of them about orders that arrived late or not at all outside the US, unexpected subscriptions and slow replies. Buy with a card or PayPal, pick the one-time purchase option, and keep your order emails.

Four styling products, each with a short ingredient list printed on its page: Sea Salt Spray (8 oz, $23.97; water, Pink Himalayan salt, gum arabic, essential oil and potassium sorbate), Hair Clay ($24.97; bentonite clay, beeswax, coconut and castor oil), Texture Powder (4 g, $22.97) and Curl Mousse (6 fl oz, $22.97). It also sells duos and kits of these, a sandalwood comb, a silicone scalp scrubber, a face towel and a valet tray.
Its About page says the products are made in the USA in a GMP-certified facility and that the brand has more than 300,000 customers. Those are the brand's own figures.

parts.small: Checked on November 24, 2026. Store ratings come from the Loox review app on simpletics.com.

parts: On the store, the Sea Salt Spray and Texture Powder hold up well across hundreds of reviews. The Hair Clay scores lower, at 3.6 from 63, and the Curl Mousse has too few reviews to judge.

Trustpilot is a different picture: 14 of the 22 reviews give one star and 6 give five. The five-star reviews praise the spray's scent and texture. The one-star reviews mostly describe orders outside the US that took weeks or months, extra charges on delivery, subscriptions buyers say they didn't notice signing up for, and emails left unanswered. Some of these reviews date from 2025, and the most recent we saw, from November 2026, was about missing tracking. It's a small sample, but the same complaints repeat.

It's a real, operating brand: it sells through a Shopify checkout, publishes shipping, refund and contact pages, and lists a US return address in Lutz, Florida. The fair worry isn't whether it exists but how it handles problems, given the Trustpilot complaints. Paying by card or PayPal gives you buyer protection, and the refund policy asks you to email support@simpletics.com within 30 days of delivery.

At $23.97 for 8 oz, the Sea Salt Spray costs about $3 an ounce, in the range of other direct-to-consumer styling sprays. The kits are where the value is: the Full Styling Kit is $57.53 against $71.91 for its three products bought alone. The 30-day guarantee on opened products lowers the risk of trying it, as long as you get a reply.

parts: Guys in the US who want a simple texture routine, a salt spray and maybe a powder or clay, with ingredient lists they can read. If you live outside the US, or you'd rather avoid any chance of a subscription mix-up, read the checkout carefully, choose the one-time purchase and keep your order confirmation.
